why: Hand-authored sources of the judge canary: one packet per golden task, stated as a real contract would state it, and one in-file edit set per defect case. `node evals/judge-canary.mjs` builds the sealed cases from this file; the label and the description never reach the judge.

tasks.objective: The write-scope decision in the tool-policy hook denies a write whose target lies outside the declared scope even when the target does not exist yet: scope membership is a fact about the path, not about the disk.
instructions: writeScopeDecision (src/host/tool-policy-decisions.mjs) stops consulting whether the target exists: a Write, Edit or NotebookEdit target outside the declared writeFiles and writeRoots is denied whether or not the file is on disk, and a declared target passes whether or not it exists.
The two read decisions keep passing a missing, unreadable or non-regular target through: a file that cannot be measured still cannot be judged.
The module header and the DECISION 1 comment state the new rule, and the helper that only served the existence check goes away.
The missing-path test asserts that creating a new file outside the scope is denied.
nonGoals: Changing the denial reason a denied write reports: its wording and the list of declared paths it shows stay as they are.
Catching writes made through Bash; the post-hoc scope gate owns those.

behaviours.text: writeScopeDecision denies a write outside the declared scope whether or not its target exists, and passes a declared target whether or not it exists.
readThresholdDecision and bashReadDecision still pass a missing or unmeasurable target through.

tasks.summary: writeScopeDecision no longer consults the disk: an out-of-scope target is denied whether or not it exists. The comments state the rule and the missing-path test asserts the denial.

tasks.objective: Pin with a regression fixture that Anthropic's soft session-limit stop normalizes to exhaustion with a reset instant, distinct from a hard stop that has none.
instructions: Add a drivers test that feeds normalizeProviderResult a claude stream ending in the session-limit error ('Claude AI usage limit reached. Your limit will reset at 2026-09-08 20:30:00') and asserts status exhausted, error code quota_exhausted, the reset text in the message, and the session id as continuation.
The same test asserts that normalizeProviderAvailability reports it unavailable with reason quota_exhausted and exhaustedUntil exactly 2026-09-08T20:30:00.000Z.
The same test contrasts it with the hard, resetless balance stop ('402 Insufficient Balance'): reason insufficient_balance and no reset instant, so the two stops are shown to differ.
nonGoals: Changing any driver or normalizer: this node adds a test only.

behaviours.text: The test pins the soft limit as exhausted with code quota_exhausted, its message and continuation id, and its exact reset instant 2026-09-08T20:30:00.000Z.
The test pins the hard balance stop as insufficient_balance with no reset instant, and shows the two stops differ.

tasks.summary: Added a drivers test pinning Anthropic's soft session limit as exhausted with its reset instant and contrasting it with the resetless 402 balance stop.

tasks.objective: normalizeCodexResult classifies a disabled code-mode host before a termination signal, and bounded codex diagnostics never exceed 512 UTF-8 bytes.
instructions: In normalizeCodexResult (scripts/drivers/exec-jsonl.mjs), classify a code-mode-host-disabled item error before the termination signal and before any later turn.completed or agent_message: a harness that dies after the host error is a provider failure (tool_host_unavailable), never a cancellation, and still reports the completed turn's usage.
A signal with no tool-host error still cancels.

boundedMessage cuts before the character that starts at the byte ceiling instead of backing up onto a dangling lead byte, so a truncated multibyte diagnostic re-encodes to at most 512 UTF-8 bytes with no U+FFFD.

The CODEX_PREAMBLE_OVERRIDES comment (scripts/drivers/codex.mjs) records all four measured host outcomes: gpt-5.6-sol 35,130 fabricated vs 35,199 correct tool-backed; deepseek-v4-flash 25,795 vs 25,783, both correct.
Regression tests pin the precedence, the byte bound and the measurements.
nonGoals: Changing how other item-level error records (rollout_budget warnings, missing model metadata) are treated: they stay ignored diagnostics.

behaviours.text: A tool-host error followed by a termination signal normalizes to a failed tool_host_unavailable envelope with the turn's usage; a signal alone still cancels.
Bounded codex diagnostics are at most 512 UTF-8 bytes and never end in a dangling multibyte sequence.
The preamble comment records the four measured host outcomes.

tasks.summary: normalizeCodexResult now classifies the tool-host error ahead of the signal, boundedMessage cuts on a character boundary, and the preamble comment records the four measurements; tests pin all three.

tasks.objective: processStartToken fingerprints a live process on darwin too, so a recycled pid is told apart from the lock holder there as it already is on Linux.
instructions: On darwin, processStartToken (scripts/lock.mjs) returns the process's start time as reported by `ps -o lstart= -p <pid>`, and null when ps fails or prints nothing.
Linux keeps reading field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat; every other platform returns null.
The processStartToken comment says where each platform's token comes from.
lock tests pin a stable darwin token for a live process, a different token for a recycled pid, a mismatch between synthetic tokens (bootstrapMatchesChild and lockStale), and null on other platforms.
nonGoals: Adding a compiled addon or requiring elevated privileges.

behaviours.text: On darwin the token is ps's lstart for the pid, null when ps fails or prints nothing.
Linux keeps its /proc token and every other platform returns null.

tasks.summary: processStartToken reads ps lstart on darwin, keeps /proc on Linux and returns null elsewhere; lock tests pin darwin stability, a recycled pid, synthetic mismatches and the other-platform null.

tasks.objective: A failing command proof with oversized output can no longer crash the controller mid-gate, a Python virtual environment no longer moves the ignore-source fingerprint, and the contract reference states what a gate costs and what it will not see.
instructions: boundedText (scripts/judge-gate.mjs) reserves the ellipsis marker's 3 bytes and shrinks until the encoded result fits, so a finding's evidence never exceeds the 4 KiB ceiling even when the cut lands inside a multibyte character.
captureIgnoreSources (scripts/verification.mjs) skips a virtual environment like node_modules: .venv and venv by name, and any directory holding pyvenv.cfg.

references/contract.md gains a section stating three gate properties: a command proof is executed at gate time under a 120-second cap; failOn ['critical'] is close to no gate at all against a judge that works at major; a worker reads only inside its worktree, so text a node must read belongs in the packet.
verification tests pin the oversized failing proof accepted by validateNodeSnapshot and the venv-neutral fingerprint.
nonGoals: Changing the 4 KiB evidence ceiling or the validator that enforces it.

behaviours.text: A failing proof's evidence is at most 4 KiB after truncation, multibyte cuts included, and the snapshot validator accepts it.
A virtual environment, by name or by its pyvenv.cfg marker, adds no ignore source.
The contract reference states all three gate properties.

tasks.summary: boundedText now reserves the marker and shrinks to fit, the ignore-source walk skips virtual environments, and contract.md documents three gate properties; verification tests pin the first two.

defects.description: The processStartToken comment says darwin reads sysctl kern.proc and falls back to the pid, while the code runs ps -o lstart= and returns null.

find: * Linux, field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat. On darwin, there is no /proc, so the
* fingerprint comes from the OS process table instead: `ps -o lstart=`
* reports the same live process's own start time on every call and a
* different one for whatever process next reuses that pid, without a
* compiled addon or elevated privileges. Every other platform has no cheap
* equivalent, so the pid probe alone decides there.
replace: * Linux, field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat. On darwin, there is no /proc, so the
* fingerprint comes from `sysctl kern.proc.pid.<pid>`, whose p_starttime is
* the same on every call for a live process and differs for whatever process
* next reuses that pid; when sysctl is unavailable the token falls back to
* the pid itself. Every other platform has no cheap equivalent, so the pid
* probe alone decides there.
